title: Al-Akhir, the Last
tomorrow: how can one verse call God both the Outward and the Inward?

cards: Nobody posts their hands after a double shift. In Medina, Fatima, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has hands worn raw from turning the stone mill.
She hears her father has received captives who could work in a household, so she goes to ask him for help. He isn't home. She leaves word with Aisha and goes back.
That night, after she and her husband Ali have lain down to sleep, someone comes to the door. It's him.

teach.b: They start to get up. He tells them to stay where they are and sits down between them; Ali remembers the coolness of his feet.
Then, as Sahih al-Bukhari tells it, he asks: shall I not teach you something better than what you asked for?
When you go to bed, say Allahu akbar thirty-four times, subhanallah thirty-three times, alhamdulillah thirty-three times. That, he says, is better for you than a servant.
It's a hard answer to hear, and the hadith doesn't pretend otherwise. She asked for help with her hands, and he gave her words for the end of the day. It doesn't say her hands stopped hurting.
It says what she was given. Why bedtime? Today's Name helps.
Al-Akhir, the Last, from the same verse as yesterday's: "He is the First and the Last."
A du'a the Prophet taught for lying down, in Sahih Muslim, says: You are the Last, and there is nothing after You.
So the day's last words go to the Last.
And one detail to tell a friend tonight: in another report, Ali says he never once dropped those bedtime words after that night.

how: Muslims who keep this hadith say subhanallah and alhamdulillah thirty-three times each and Allahu akbar thirty-four times before sleep, counting on their fingers or on prayer beads.

o: the Judge on the very last day
the Last, with nothing after Him
the one who sends the final prophet

games.q: who did what that night — tap the pairs.
p: felt the coolness of his feet

s: the Prophet gave Fatima the servant she asked for
he gave her bedtime words instead, and called them better for her than a servant.
the hadith says her hands healed after that night
it doesn't say. it says what she was given.
a bedtime du'a calls Allah the Last, with nothing after Him
in Sahih Muslim: You are the Last, and there is nothing after You.

games.q: you're at the door that night. Fatima asked her father for help with the work. what does he give her?
o: a servant from the captives, since she asked first
words to say at bedtime, which he calls better
advice to grind less grain each day
games.why: he sat between them and taught the bedtime words: thirty-four, thirty-three, thirty-three. better for you than a servant, he said.

practice: Count slowly on your fingers: subhanallah, glory be to God; alhamdulillah, praise be to God; Allahu akbar, God is greatest. Don't race for the number. Go as far as the sit allows, as if these were the last words of your day.

wordCard.voice: Al-Akhir. The Last, after everything, with nothing after Him: the Name that gets the day's final words.

orig.note: Arabic: the Last. the second of the four Names in 57:3.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: last, the One who stays when the lights go off. Sleep well when it's time.
